figures.finding: For UK television, Pact and Directors UK have a Directors Rights, Administration, Payment and Reporting Agreement (2020), which Pact describes as setting the rights and minimum terms for engaging directors in TV; its text and any fee figures are open to Pact members only.

value.name: Directors UK (DUK) Directors Rights, Administration, Payment and Reporting Agreement

figures.applies: UK, independent producers in Pact engaging directors on television; the terms themselves were not readable on 2026-11-01.

sources.said: Directors Rights, Administration, Payment and Reporting Agreement 2020 Application: This agreement covers the rights and minimum terms for engaging directors in TV.
This content is only available to Pact members.

figures.finding: For feature films there is no collective fee agreement: Directors UK's Creative Rights Minimum Terms for Fiction Feature Film (launched 2017, supported by Pact, the BFI, BBC Films and Film4) are terms directors and agents are asked to write into each contract, covering prep, production and post-production rights rather than pay.

value.name: Creative Rights Minimum Terms for Fiction Feature Film
value.binding: only as written into each director's contract

figures.applies: UK fiction feature films; the terms document itself (hosted on a CDN this environment's proxy refused) was not read, so its clauses are not modelled.

sources.said: Directors UK has today launched the new Creative Rights Minimum Terms following extensive consultation with directors themselves and with key industry stakeholders including Pact, the BFI, the British Film Commissioner, BBC Films, Channel Four Films, the Production Guild and the agents’ body the Personal Managers Association. UK film directors and their agents will require these to be incorporated in their contracts for all fiction feature films.
The core set or requirements will allow a director to execute his or her work in the most efficient way during prep, production and post-production.

figures.finding: Directors UK, the UK screen directors' body, has over 8,500 members and pays rights payments; joining starts from a principal director credit on a broadcast UK television programme or a commercially distributed feature.

value.entryTest: principal director credit on a broadcast UK TV programme or commercially distributed and screened feature film

sources.said: We support over 8,500 members, distributing rights payments, representing their vision in government and protecting the director’s craft.
Do you have a principal director credit on a broadcast UK television programme, or commercially distributed and screened feature film?

figures.finding: English is the working language: in the 2021 Census 91.1% of residents of England and Wales aged three and over had English (or Welsh in Wales) as their main language.
figures.applies: England and Wales, Census 2021 (Scotland and Northern Ireland not included in this release).

sources.said: In 2021, 91.1% (52.6 million) of usual residents, aged three years and over, had English (English or Welsh in Wales) as a main language (down from 92.3%, or 49.8 million, in 2011).

figures.finding: London is the centre of the work: Creative England counted £3.14bn of high-end TV and £5.12bn of film production spend in Metro London (with Hertfordshire, Buckinghamshire and Surrey) in 2017-2019, against £1.8bn across the English regions outside London.
figures.applies: England, film and high-end TV production spend 2017-2019, Creative England's Powering Economic Growth & Opportunity Across the Regions report as quoted by KFTV (25 February 2022).

sources.said: However, the figures demonstrate that London and the surrounding area continues to capture the lion’s share of spend. Metro London attracted £3.14bn of high-end TV production spend in the period. … By comparison, Metro London drew £5.12bn of film production spend in the same period. … High-end TV and film production spend in the English regions hit £1.8bn between 2017 and 2019, according to Creative England.

figures.finding: Bectu, the union for UK screen crew (directors among them), charges dues by gross annual earnings in 2026: £120 a year on £12,501-15,000, rising by band to £309.96 on £32,501-35,000 and £350.04 on £35,001 and above.
